subject: Logic
title: The Contrapositive
description: A fast breakdown of The Contrapositive for builders.

hook.text: "If it rains, the ground is wet" means exactly the same as "If the ground is dry, it didn't rain."

buildup.text: The contrapositive of P → Q is ¬Q → ¬P. Flip both parts and negate them. Always equivalent.

discovery.text: The converse (Q → P) is NOT equivalent. "If the ground is wet, it rained" could be wrong—sprinklers.

twist.text: The inverse (¬P → ¬Q) also fails equivalence. Only the contrapositive preserves truth perfectly.

climax.text: Contrapositive reasoning is a proof technique: prove the contrapositive to prove the original.

quiz.question: What is the contrapositive of 'If P then Q'?
options: If not Q then not P
If not P then not Q
